item.title: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Jensen, David I Ketcheson, Lajos L\'oczi

item.title: Geometric multigrid preconditioners for unfitted discretisations of the de Rham complex
item.description: arXiv:2610.22865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose two families of multigrid preconditioners for unfitted finite element discretisations of the Riesz maps of the de Rham complex, in H(grad), H(curl) and H(div), stabilised by cell aggregation. The first is a geometric multigrid method applied directly to the unfitted operators, on a hierarchy of background meshes that share the same boundary representation. Its smoothers are star patches built on the aggregated mesh, so that each patch captures the kernel of the stabilisation. The second is a multilevel auxiliary-space preconditioner that combines a patch smoother localised around the cut cells with the body-fitted problem on the active mesh, which is in turn solved by a non-nested geometric multigrid method. Both are used as building blocks of block-diagonal preconditioners for the mixed Hodge Laplacians. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on geometries with a controlled cut fraction and on general geometries, show iteration counts that are robust with respect to the cut configuration, the mesh size and the number of levels. We also report results for higher-order discretisations, weakly imposed Dirichlet boundary conditions and a face-based stabilisation.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Badia, Jordi Manyer

item.title: Geometry-Aware Latent Representation Learning for Drag Coefficient Prediction of Irregular Particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.23087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting the drag coefficient $C_\mathrm{d}$ of irregular particles requires representing their complex three-dimensional geometry in a form suitable for predictive models. Empirical drag correlations and many data-driven models represent particle geometry through a small set of hand-crafted shape descriptors. Geometric differences omitted by these descriptors are unavailable to the predictor. We propose a variational autoencoder-multilayer perceptron (VAE-MLP) framework that learns a latent representation directly from voxelized particle geometry. Geometry reconstruction and drag coefficient prediction jointly guide the learning of this representation. We compare VAE-MLP with a descriptor-based MLP (Descriptor-MLP) and established empirical correlations using CFD data for synthetic particle geometries at Reynolds numbers of 10--200. When the evaluated geometric variations are represented in the training data, the two learned models achieve comparable accuracy for regular ellipsoids, while VAE-MLP yields lower errors for irregular particles. When high-order surface perturbations are excluded from training, VAE-MLP achieves lower overall mean absolute relative error in all five training runs. At the strongest tested perturbation, the mean errors across these runs are 4.97% for VAE-MLP and 9.88% for Descriptor-MLP. These results support learning geometric representations directly from particle geometry to improve drag prediction for the irregular geometries and unseen surface perturbations examined here.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Li, Shota Deguchi, Mitsuteru Asai, Shunhua Chen, Naoto Mitsume

item.title: Stability and Error Estimates for Convolution Quadrature under Radial Symbol Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop stability and error estimates for multistep convolution quadrature (CQ) under general radial bounds on the Laplace symbol. Instead of the classical single-power condition $|F(z)|\leq M|z|^{-\mu}$, we assume $|F(z)|\leq C\Phi(|z|)$ and consider two classes of radial functions: monotone bounds satisfying a scaling condition and regularly varying bounds with locally bounded above and away from zero. For strongly $A(\alpha)$-stable multistep methods, we derive approximation and stability estimates for the CQ weights, as well as error bounds for power-type inputs $g_\beta(t)=t^{\beta-1}/\Gamma(\beta)$ with $\beta>0$. These estimates explicitly retain the dependence on the memory law through the factor $\Phi(t_n^{-1})$. The framework accommodates symbols whose behavior cannot be described by a global single-power. It also preserves slowly varying and multiscale factors that would be lost under a coarser power majorant. The theory is applied to fractional viscoelastic models, distributed-order operators, and logarithmic-power memory operators. Numerical experiments with backward Euler and second-order backward differentiation CQ confirm the expected temporal convergence orders for direct responses. Complementary evolution examples demonstrate the corresponding temporal behavior for smooth and nonsmooth initial data.
item.dc:creator: Jingchuang Ren, Haibin Su

item.title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities and Uncertainty Quantification in a Morphoelastic Model for Burn Injury Healing
item.description: arXiv:2610.23177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematical modelling of burn injury healing involves coupling biological processes with mechanical deformation, resulting in computationally stiff, nonlinear partial differential equations that severely limit the scalability of existing numerical solutions. We present a computational framework addressing these challenges. By nondimensionalizing the model and performing scaling analysis, we show that chemotaxis and inertia are negligible, permitting a quasi-static momentum approach. To enforce non-negativity constraints, we implement a Variational Inequality formulation using the Finite Element Method in FEniCSx, and verify it via numerical convergence studies and mass balances. We identify high-order parameter interactions, specifically equilibrium collagen density and signalling dynamics, as the primary drivers of solver stability. A sensitivity analysis of nearly four million simulations reveals that isolated parameter variations predominantly govern the maximum wound contraction. In contrast, higher-order interactions determine the timing of maximum contraction and the permanent contracture. However, no significant pairwise parameter interactions were found, suggesting that the model's behaviour is governed by higher-order interactions, highlighting the inherent complexity of the wound-healing process.
item.dc:creator: Wilbert den Hertog, Fred Vermolen

item.title: Multilevel Gaussian Processes with Applications to Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.23202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a multilevel Gaussian process (GP) regression framework for approximating functions that are accessible only through a hierarchy of approximations of increasing accuracy and computational cost. One example is the response surface of a parametrized partial differential equation, where the hierarchy arises from the resolution of the numerical solver. Modeling level increments independently with Mat\'ern-kernel GPs and allocating samples flexibly across discretization levels yields substantial computational savings over single-level GP regression. We derive $L^2$ convergence rates for the posterior mean and variance, accounting for maximum likelihood estimation of the marginal variance and for kernel misspecification. When increment regularity or solver cost is unknown a priori, an adaptive sequential-design algorithm with cost-adapted active learning criteria allocates samples across levels. We apply the surrogate to Bayesian inverse problems, for which Hellinger distance bounds between the true and approximate posteriors are known. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical rates and the resulting computational savings.
item.dc:creator: Stjepan Salatovic, Aretha L. Teckentrup, Sebastian Krumscheid

item.title: A configurational numerical viscosity for thermodynamically compatible finite volume schemes of compressible multiphase flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.23247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the fluid subsystem of a variationally derived hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (HTC) model of compressible multiphase flows. Its total energy is in general not convex in the natural state variables, so a scalar numerical viscosity acting on them need not produce non-negative entropy. Reformulating the equations in terms of the volume fractions separates changes in the amount of each phase from changes in its intrinsic state. This guides the construction of a configurational numerical viscosity in phase variables, in which the energy is convex, while the scheme retains the structure of the HTC model. At the semi-discrete level, the new schemes satisfy: I) local conservation of the phase masses, the mixture momentum and the total energy; II) a cell entropy inequality whose production is non-negative face by face and phase by phase, with no convexity assumption in the evolved variables and no clipping; III) positivity of the partial densities and volume fractions under explicit time-step conditions; IV) exact preservation of contact equilibria; V) equivalence with a scheme for the density-weighted volume fractions. The key ingredients are: i) an exact decomposition of the jump of each phase across a face into a configurational part, dissipated with the material speed, and an intrinsic part, dissipated with the acoustic speed; ii) an exchange form of this dissipation between neighbouring cells, with non-negative weights; iii) a side-wise transfer of the dissipation to the evolved variables through the chain rule of each cell, which turns the energy defects into Bregman divergences of the single-fluid energies; iv) a thermodynamic correction of the reversible part built in the phase variables. Properties I)-V) are proved and verified numerically, including a shock tube in which the Rusanov viscosity produces negative entropy and a shock-water column interaction.
item.dc:creator: Davide Ferrari, Ilya Peshkov, Michael Dumbser

item.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo based meshfree methods for parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a randomized path sampling framework for the pointwise approximation of linear parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds, treating both closed manifolds and manifolds with Dirichlet boundary. Based on the Feynman-Kac representation, we construct a parameter-coordinate retraction-based discretization, referred to as the p-Ret scheme, for the manifold diffusion generated by the uniformly elliptic operator, and use it to formulate the Monte Carlo (MC) and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC) methods. We derive the local weak consistency of the p-Ret transition and first-order weak convergence of the temporal discretization on closed manifolds. For fixed $h$, we show that RQMC sampling yields asymptotically faster variance decay than standard MC. On closed manifolds, the variance is $o(n^{-1})$ and, under additional regularity, satisfies the sharper bound $O(n^{-2+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. For Dirichlet problems, despite the discontinuities induced by numerical first exit, nested-uniformly scrambled Sobol' sampling attains $O(n^{-1-1/s+\varepsilon})$ variance for any $\varepsilon>0$ under suitable regularity assumptions, where $s$ denotes the nominal path-space dimension. More notably, we further develop an Array-RQMC strategy based on stepwise low-dimensional randomized point sets and a Hilbert space-filling curve that maps high-dimensional particle states to a one-dimensional ordering, and establish a variance rate of $o(n^{-1})$ under suitable assumptions. Numerical results demonstrate that both RQMC methods reduce variance and root mean square error (RMSE) relative to standard MC and remain effective for manifolds with intrinsic dimension up to $50$.
item.dc:creator: Zhijian He, Zhiyuan Hui, Changtao Sheng, Bihao Su, Tao Zhou

item.title: Explicit Oblique Inverses of the Approximate Discrete Radon Transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.23363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The approximate discrete Radon transform (ADRT) is a fast, hierarchical approximation of the Radon transform whose levels have explicit spectral decompositions, but its Moore-Penrose inverse, needed for data outside the range, has no closed form. We construct explicit left inverses of the ADRT, oblique projections onto its range, that are exact for every choice of their parameters and amplify noise by a constant factor relative to the Moore-Penrose inverse. Realized with polynomial filters on the butterfly structure of the levels, they are fixed linear maps of cost $O(N^{5/2}\log^{3/2}N/\sigma_{\min})$ for an $N\times N$ image, where $\sigma_{\min}$ is the smallest singular value of the ADRT; with the measured growth $\sigma_{\min}\sim N^{1/4}$ this is $O(N^{2.25}\log^{3/2}N)$. A hybrid that keeps the explicit inverse of the cross-quadrant level is cheaper and closer to the Moore-Penrose inverse. In compiled implementations both outperform a polynomial solver of the normal equations from $N=256$ on, and their conditioning is traced to the aliasing of integer-sampled lines.
item.dc:creator: Donsub Rim

item.title: Accelerated Born series for high-frequency strong scattering by weakly non-radial media
item.description: arXiv:2610.23428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a practical method for accelerating the modified Born series for high-frequency Helmholtz scattering in one, two, and three dimensions. We consider bounded, nonnegative, compactly supported media, allowing small departures from radial symmetry in two and three dimensions. The method selects a single complex relaxation parameter using an approximation of the scattering operator's spectrum. Starting from precomputed eigenvalues for a constant reference medium, we estimate their evolution towards the prescribed radial profile. A leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation reduces this spectral propagation to scalar nonlinear equations, followed by a first-order correction for the nonradial part of the medium. The estimated eigenvalues, together with a bound on the omitted spectrum, define a convex minimax problem for selecting the relaxation parameter. This spectral preparation is independent of the source and can therefore be reused for multiple scattering problems in the same medium. Numerical examples demonstrate convergence in strongly scattering cases where the scattering operator has spectral radius greater than one. Comparisons with direct integral-equation and finite-difference solvers assess accuracy, residual convergence, and computation time, and show computational savings at comparable accuracy in selected examples.
item.dc:creator: Mirza Karamehmedovi\'c, Faouzi Triki

item.title: Fast matrix-vector products in tensor-train format via structured sketching
item.description: arXiv:2610.23451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a randomized, streamable algorithm that computes a tensor-train approximation of a matrix-vector product without ever forming the full intermediate tensor. We develop three contraction strategies for streaming tensor-train approximation (STTA): sequential, fused, and pre-sketched. We focus on the regime of large operator mode sizes and show that pre-sketching can provide significant speed-ups when a lower-rank approximation of the input is sought, by pre-computing all sketch-related contractions with the operator. The pre-sketched strategy can also accelerate successive randomized compression (SRC), although to a lesser extent since its second sweep depends on the input vector and cannot be pre-computed. We compare the three strategies in terms of computational cost and memory, and demonstrate their performance on synthetic and application-driven examples where rank reduction is relevant.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Bucci, Stefan G\"uttel, John W. Pearson

item.title: A Structure-Preserving Semi-Lagrangian based bi-fidelity method for the Vlasov--Poisson system with uncertainties
item.description: arXiv:2610.23484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncertainty quantification for the Vlasov--Poisson (VP) systems entails repeated dynamic simulations, incurring immense computational costs. We develop a structure-preserving Semi-Lagrangian (SL) b-fidelity approximation of macroscopic observables. The MUSCL is used as a low-fidelity solver for pressureless Euler--Poisson system, allowing for a more cost-effective exploration of the stochastic parameter space. A conservative SL scheme combined with high-order discontinuous Galerkin is used as a high-fidelity solver for collisionless VP system, whose mass conservation, positivity preservation, and low numerical dissipation provide a more reliable high-fidelity snapshots for bi-fidelity reconstruction. We further derive a conditional error bound that separates projection, discretization, and model errors. Numerical experiments for both deterministic and uncertain VP problems, including multispecies and higher-dimensional settings, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and robust uncertainty propagation.
item.dc:creator: Xiaofeng Cai, Jiaojiao Guo, Liu Liu

item.title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.23492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the biharmonic problem on closed smooth surfaces, we construct a nonconforming finite element method that requires neither stabilization nor the Piola transform. The reduced enriched quartic (REQ) element relies solely on vertex values and scalar edge moments. The same local construction applies to every triangle of a piecewise planar surface. The bilinear form consists of elementwise Laplacian inner products and permits standard finite element assembly. By separating the planar vertex residual from the angle defect contribution, we establish weak discrete Miranda--Talenti-type estimates on both planar meshes and closed piecewise planar surfaces. These estimates guarantee uniform stability on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes. We prove the well-posedness of the method, first-order convergence in the energy norm, and second-order convergence in the broken $H^1$ and $L^2$ norms. Numerical tests on three surfaces show the predicted convergence rates and examine the discrete Miranda--Talenti constants and angle defect scaling.
item.dc:creator: Jiachen Gu, Xia Ji, Shuo Zhang

item.title: A Mixed Elliptic--Hyperbolic Monge--Amp\`ere Problem: Modeling and a Least-Squares Solver
item.description: arXiv:2610.23544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a transport problem motivated by freeform optical design of a parallel-to-far-field reflector. Classical formulations rely on either elliptic or hyperbolic Monge--Amp\`ere equations, leading to globally convex/concave or saddle-shape reflector geometries, respectively. However, the design of smooth reflector arrays may require optical surfaces combining both types of curvature. To address this, we introduce a mixed elliptic--hyperbolic Monge--Amp\`ere system obtained by partitioning the source domain into one elliptic and one hyperbolic subregion, and we develop a least-squares method for its numerical approximation. Numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to compute both isolated and periodic mixed-type transport solutions, yielding smooth reflector configurations.
item.dc:creator: G. V. Carvalho, M. J. H. Anthonissen, J. H. M. ten Thije Boonkkamp, L. Kusch, W. L. IJzerman

item.title: Toward Spectral Deferred Correction Methods for Stochastic Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numerical solution of stochastic differential equations is computationally very demanding. Often it is of interest to evaluate certain moments, e.g., the expectation, by Monte Carlo sampling, thus requiring the computation of numerous realizations. The discretization error of the numerical scheme induces bias in the computed Monte Carlo estimator. As popular numerical schemes, like Euler-Maruyama or Milstein, are low-order, even reasonably coarse error bounds for the simulation are costly to achieve. While the evaluation of moments requires only weak convergence, in other applications like parameter estimation, strong convergence is important, but higher-order is typically harder to obtain in the strong than in the weak sense. In this paper we develop an efficient method with the potential of achieving higher strong and weak convergence order. It is based on the smooth approximation of Brownian bridges combined with spectral deferred correction methods well known for the numerical solution of ordinary differential equations. We discuss convergence, and present numerical results.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Binkowski, Matthew R. Christian, Sebastian G\"otschel, Michael L. Minion

item.title: Error analysis of a backward L2 method on graded meshes for linear and semilinear subdiffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-fractional linear and semilinear parabolic equations with a Caputo time derivative of order $\alpha\in(0,1)$ are considered. Their solutions exhibit an initial singularity of type $t^\sigma$ for any fixed $\sigma \in (0,1) \cup (1,2)$. A backward L2-type discrete fractional-derivative operator of order $3-\alpha$ is considered on nonuniform temporal meshes. Sufficient conditions for inverse monotonicity of this operator areestablished. Hence, sharp pointwise-in-time error bounds are obtained on graded temporal meshes with arbitrary degree of grading. The theoretical findings are illustrated by numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Kopteva, Lu Wang

item.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
item.description: arXiv:2610.22658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $\gamma = n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $\gamma$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Ioana Dumitriu, Hai-Xiao Wang

item.title: Optimal approximation of smooth functions by ReLU neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.22693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study uniform approximation of the H\"older ball $\mathcal H_1^s([0,1]^D)$ by fully connected ReLU networks. Except in the one-dimensional Lipschitz case, existing constructions remain separated from the information-theoretic efficiency limit. This article closes the gap for every $s>0$ and $D\ge1$: networks with width $O(N)$, depth $O(L)$, and parameter magnitude $O(1)$ attain uniform approximation error of order $(N^2L^2\log N)^{-s/D}$. No relation between width and depth is required. The construction uses new encoding and decoding mechanisms that exploit higher-order finite-difference bounds for local Taylor coefficients of the target function. As a statistical consequence, empirical risk minimizers over the corresponding clipped network classes attain the minimax regression rate $n^{-2s/(2s+D)}$ without additional logarithmic factors. The paper also gives a detailed exposition of the key approximation techniques, covering both established and new mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Nagler

item.title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.22903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) faces significant challenges when solving compressible multi-medium flows, including the inability to locate interface positions, poor approximation of discontinuities, and difficulty in handling high-pressure-ratio problems between media with large stiffness differences. To address these issues, we propose PINN with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition (PINN-LPCDD), a framework that incorporates the sharp interface method (SIM) into PINNs for solving compressible multi-medium flows. Firstly, we design separate sub-networks for each medium with learnable parameters to automatically learn interface positions, so that the domain decomposition is physically consistent, and the contact discontinuity at the interface is naturally sharp. Secondly, the Euler equations with artificial viscosity are solved to enhance robustness when handling problems involving shock waves. Lastly, the scaling invariance of the Euler equations is exploited to facilitate the solution of high pressure ratio problems. Numerical experiments on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 problems demonstrate the acceptable accuracy of the proposed method in simulating multi-medium flows.
item.dc:creator: Weiheng Zeng, Hao Wang, Jiaxin Zhu, Kun Wang, Tiegang Liu, Chengliang Feng

item.title: Convergence rate of stochastic gradient descent under {\L}ojasiewicz type condition and polynomially controlled noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.23386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic gradient methods are widely used for solving optimization problems in many scientific fields. Recently, their popularity has risen due to the increase in machine learning's prominence. Their convergence is often studied under the convexity assumption, which is too restrictive in modern applications. In this paper, we investigate the almost sure convergence rate and expectation under a {\L}ojasiewicz-type gradient domination condition. This framework includes both bounded and decaying noise, as well as noise with controlled polynomial growth. The obtained results extend existing convergence by allowing a broader class of noise sequences and explicitly capturing the effect of their asymptotic behavior on the convergence rate and applicability.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} W\k{e}grzyn

item.title: Cayley access models for matrix functions: reachable class and cost
item.description: arXiv:2610.23429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how to compute $f(A)b$ on a quantum computer, where $A$ is Hermitian. When $f$ is nonsmooth or has localized difficulty in the spectrum, classical numerical linear algebra approximates it with rational functions rather than polynomials. We propose the Cayley transform, parameterized by $\sigma \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\gamma > 0$, as an alternative to the standard quantum access model. The two parameters let one concentrate accuracy where $f$ is difficult, which standard models can achieve only by raising the polynomial degree globally. This transformation converts Hermitian matrices to unitaries, allowing generalized quantum signal processing to apply Laurent polynomials bounded on the unit circle. We compare three access models (block encoding, matrix exponential, and Cayley encoding) in terms of query complexity and of the cost of their circuit realization. When the difficulty of $f$ is localized in the spectrum, the Cayley encoding reduces the required degree by a factor of three to four, and it represents the shifted resolvent exactly at degree one. For spectral projectors, the standard models cannot reach the target accuracy at fixed degree, because their approximants cannot concentrate resolution near the discontinuity. Realizing the Cayley encoding from a block encoding requires solving a shifted linear system, whose cost offsets its query-complexity gain over the standard models. For structured matrices arising in practice, however, low-depth circuits for the encoding can be constructed directly, and the gain is preserved at the circuit level.
item.dc:creator: Gianna M. Del Corso

item.title: Optimal convergence rates for the finite element approximation of the Sobolev constant
item.description: arXiv:2504.09637v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates for the continuous piecewise affine finite element approximation of the Sobolev constant in arbitrary dimensions N\geq 2 and for Lebesgue exponents 1<p<N. Our analysis relies on a refined study of the Sobolev deficit in suitable quasi-norms, which have been introduced and utilized in the context of finite element approximations of the p-Laplacian. The proof further involves sharp estimates for the finite element approximation of Sobolev minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Liviu I. Ignat, Enrique Zuazua

item.title: Derivation and Numerical Simulation of a Thermodynamically Consistent Magneto Two-phase Flow Model
item.description: arXiv:2508.04360v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by Magnetic Drug Targeting (MDT), we derive a thermodynamically consistent two-phase model for the coupled dynamics of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), a carrier fluid, and the magnetic field. The model includes a convection-diffusion equation for the SPION dispersion volume density and a modified Navier-Stokes system for the mixture velocity with SPION-dependent density and viscosity, an additional momentum flux due to relative SPION motion, and a magnetic body force. Additionally, the SPIONs interact with a quasi-static Maxwell system through their magnetization which is of Langevin type. The coupled system satisfies a global energy-dissipation balance. Moreover, we develop a semi-implicit finite element scheme with explicit flux-corrected transport stabilization and simulate the attraction of an initially localized SPION dispersion towards an external magnet in a system closed to mass exchange, using parameter values representative of MDT settings. The resulting SPION redistribution and induced flow are analyzed through physical observables, including energy and dissipation contributions and iron mass within a target region. Temporal convergence studies assess the ability of the numerical scheme to reproduce the energy-dissipation balance. Finally, we study the influence of individual coupling mechanisms on particle accumulation, maximum iron density, and peak flow velocity.
item.dc:creator: Eberhard B\"ansch, Jonas Knoch, Nicolas Neuss, Maria Neuss-Radu

item.title: Optimization of gridding algorithms for FFT by vector optimization
item.description: arXiv:2512.14914v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is widely used in applications such as MRI, CT, and interferometry; however, because of its dependence on uniformly sampled data, it requires the use of gridding techniques for practical implementation. The performance of these algorithms strongly depends on the choice of the gridding kernel, with the first prolate spheroidal wave function (PSWF) regarded as optimal. This work redefines kernel optimality through the lens of vector optimization (VO), introducing a rigorous framework that characterizes optimal kernels as Pareto-efficient solutions of an error shape operator. We establish the continuity of such operator, study the existence of solutions, and propose a novel methodology to construct kernels tailored to a desired target error function. The approach is implemented numerically via interior-point optimization. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed kernels outperform both the PSWF and the state-of-the-art methods (MIRT-NUFFT) in specific regions of interest, achieving orders-of-magnitude improvements in mean absolute errors. These results confirm the potential of VO-based kernel design to provide customized accuracy profiles aligned with application-specific requirements. Future research will extend this framework to multidimensional cases and relative error minimization, with potential integration of machine learning for adaptive target error selection.
item.dc:creator: Federico Achini, Paola Causin, Sara Vanini, Ke Chen, Simone Scacchi

item.title: Multilevel Neural Corrections with Adaptive Sampling for Partial Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2601.12000v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a multi-level framework for deep neural PDE solvers that integrates adaptive sampling with additive neural corrections. At each level, an adaptive sampling distribution is constructed from normalized residual-gradient indicators inherited from the preceding levels, thereby concentrating collocation points in regions where the current approximation exhibits large local errors or reduced regularity. The neural approximations obtained at previous levels are incorporated into a successive correction problem, leading to a hierarchical refinement of the numerical solution. Under suitable assumptions, we establish rigorous approximation results and derive error bounds for the proposed multi-level framework, which quantify the cumulative effect of the successive neural corrections across levels. Numerical experiments on representative PDEs with steep gradients and low-regularity solutions demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive multi-level strategy.
item.dc:creator: Yu Yang, Qiaolin He

item.title: On the convergence rates of generalized conditional gradient method for fully discretized Mean Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2602.11640v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study convergence rates of the generalized conditional gradient (GCG) method applied to fully discretized Mean Field Games (MFG) systems. While explicit convergence rates of the GCG method have been established at the continuous PDE level, a rigorous analysis that simultaneously accounts for time-space discretization and iteration errors has been missing. In this work, we consider an MFG system with a quadratic Hamiltonian including an advection term. We employ the GCG method to construct an iterative algorithm in which the HJB and FP equations are solved separately. At each iteration, we apply the Cole--Hopf transformation to linearize these equations and discretize the resulting linear PDEs using a finite difference method. We then analyze the resulting fully discrete GCG scheme. Under suitable structural assumptions on coupling terms, we establish discrete maximum principles and derive explicit error estimates that quantify both discretization errors and iteration errors within a unified framework. Our estimates show how the convergence rates depend on the mesh sizes and the iteration number, and they reveal a non-uniform behavior with respect to the iteration. Moreover, we prove that higher convergence rates can be achieved under additional regularity assumptions on the solution. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the theoretical results and to confirm the predicted convergence behavior.
item.dc:creator: Haruka Nakamura, Norikazu Saito

item.title: A boundary integral equation method for Steklov eigenvalue problems for smooth planar domains
item.description: arXiv:2604.05975v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we present a novel numerical method for computing the Steklov spectrum of bounded and unbounded simply connected planar domains with smooth boundaries. For the unit disk, the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator can be written explicitly in terms of the classical conjugation operator. We extend this framework to general simply connected domains by expressing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator in terms of the generalized conjugation operator, which is defined via the boundary integral equation with the generalized Neumann kernel. Combined with Fourier differentiation on an equidistant boundary grid, this approach leads to a dense algebraic eigenvalue problem for the boundary traces of the Steklov eigenfunctions. The resulting method is simple, highly accurate, and uses only boundary data. It treats interior and exterior problems in a unified manner and reconstructs eigenfunctions inside the domain using the Cauchy integral formula. Numerical experiments on benchmark domains and parameter-dependent smooth families, including ellipses and star-like curves, demonstrate high accuracy and illustrate how the Steklov spectrum changes with geometry.
item.dc:creator: Jamie Swan, Mohamed M. S. Nasser, Harri Hakula, Matti Vuorinen

item.title: Conditioning and backward errors for nonlinear eigenvalue problems with eigenvector nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2605.20933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider eigenvalue condition numbers and backward errors for a class of symmetric nonlinear eigenvalue problems with eigenvector nonlinearities. For both of these quantities, we derive explicit and computable expressions that can be evaluated with little computational effort for a given eigenpair, assuming the matrix perturbations are measured by the spectral or Frobenius norm. We also show how symmetric perturbations can be exploited in the analysis. By means of two numerical experiments we demonstrate that problems incorporating eigenvector nonlinearities potentially need to be treated with additional care, when compared to the linear or eigenvalue-nonlinear theory.
item.dc:creator: Vilhelm Peterson Lithell, Victor Janssens, Elias Jarlebring, Karl Meerbergen, Wim Michiels

item.title: Dynamic inverse problems: Online regularisation theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.26022v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop regularisation theory for dynamic inverse problems, solved using online methods with an infinite time horizon. Using concepts of subregularity to treat nonsmooth regularisers, we prove that time-averaged reconstruction errors converge to zero as noise, algorithmic errors, and regularisation vanish as the horizon grows. We illustrate the theory numerically with a dynamic electrical impedance tomography example.
item.dc:creator: Jyrki Jauhiainen, Yassine Nabou, Tuomo Valkonen

item.title: Exact-curved Lagrange finite elements for the Poisson problem in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2605.26566v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Conforming mapped Lagrange finite elements of any fixed degree are analysed for the Poisson problem on exact curved triangulations in two dimensions. The element map is factorised into an anisotropic affine core map and a smooth curved correction. Assuming compatible edge parametrisations, semi-regular affine cores and uniform bounds on the curved corrections, we obtain anisotropic $L^2$- and $H^1$-interpolation estimates with constants independent of the aspect ratios of the cores. The estimates retain lower-order terms induced by the non-affine maps, and these terms cannot be omitted in general. For sufficiently regular solutions, the Galerkin errors on the exact domain converge with the optimal orders in the energy norm and, on convex domains, in the $L^2$ norm. A fixed smooth diffeomorphism maps a semi-regular family of polygonal triangulations to exact curved triangulations satisfying these assumptions, even when the core aspect ratios are unbounded. An explicit family with an exact circular boundary arc is given. Numerical experiments with linear and quadratic elements confirm the predicted rates. At a fixed horizontal mesh width, the errors remain bounded as the aspect ratio increases.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Ishizaka

item.title: Elastic wave propagation in fractured media with spring-type and frictional contact deformation laws
item.description: arXiv:2608.16460v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Elastic wave propagation in fractured media is relevant to applications such as analysis of seismic waves and non-destructive characterization of materials. Understanding attenuation and scattering behavior arising from wave-fracture interaction is important for interpreting observations at both field and laboratory scales. This work presents a computational method for elastic wave propagation in fractured media based on a mixed-dimensional discrete fracture-matrix representation. Fracture deformation is governed by four models of increasing complexity, ranging from widely used spring-based formulations to frictional fracture contact models. Many previous studies are restricted to simplified wave fields, single fractures or subsets of the relevant fracture deformation mechanisms. In contrast, the proposed methodology enables fully coupled simulation of elastic wave propagation with fracture deformation models that account for elastic normal deformation, frictional contact and fracture opening and closure. The elastic wave equation is discretized in space using the cell-centered finite volume method Multi-Point Stress Approximation with weak symmetry and in time using the Newmark method. The spatial discretization is locally conservative and applicable to general polyhedral grids, making it well suited for media containing fractures, material heterogeneities and anisotropy. The proposed methodology is verified through numerical convergence analyses and is subsequently applied to wave propagation and fracture deformation in two- and three-dimensional media containing multiple intersecting fractures, demonstrating the influence of fracture constitutive behavior on wave transmission, scattering and fracture deformation.
item.dc:creator: Ingrid Kristine Jacobsen, Jan Martin Nordbotten, Ivar Stefansson, Barbara Wohlmuth, Inga Berre

item.title: A Fast Nonuniform Solver for the Poisson Equation over a Disk
item.description: arXiv:2609.40344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study fast numerical methods for the Poisson equation on a disk within the FFTRR (Fast Fourier Transform Radial Recurrence) framework, which is built on Green's function representations. Classical FFTRR schemes apply FFTs in the azimuthal variable and evaluate mode-by-mode radial recurrences, achieving a complexity of \(O(MN\log N)\) on an \(N\times M\) uniform grid. However, they require a uniformly spaced azimuthal mesh of \(N\) points. In this work we develop a Nonuniform (NUFFTRR) solver that admits nonuniform grids in both the radial and azimuthal directions while retaining the favorable structure of the original FFTRR formulation. The azimuthal analysis-synthesis step is implemented using either a dense NUDFT least-squares solver or one of two NUFFT-based iterative schemes: a Toeplitz solver using circulant-preconditioned conjugate gradients (PCG), and a preconditioned conjugate gradient for least squares (PCGLS) solver with Pipe--Menon density compensation. These yield azimuthal complexities \(O(N^3 + MN^2)\) for the NUDFT variant and \(O(K_{\mathrm{iter}} MN\log N)\) for the NUFFT-based variants on an \(N\times M\) grid and Krylov iteration count \(K_{\mathrm{iter}}\). Numerical experiments on nonuniform meshes demonstrate that the proposed method is robust, spectrally accurate in the azimuthal variable, and competitive in runtime with existing fast Poisson solvers. We make use of vectorization and batched BLAS/GPU-accelerated linear algebra operations to eliminate explicit loops while also formulating azimuthal and radial steps entirely in terms of dense array operations, FFTs, and NUFFTs, allowing for straightforward GPU acceleration. The implementation is released as an open-source Python package at https://github.com/CharliePyle4/NUFFTRR_Poisson, and its methodology can be extended directly to related elliptic problems such as the Helmholtz equation.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Pyle, Prabir Daripa

item.title: Latent Evolution Operator (LEO): State-to-State Forecasting of Parametric PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2505.09063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solving time-dependent parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) with high-fidelity solvers is expensive in multi-query settings. This motivates reduced-order models in latent space. Existing methods are typically either (i) recurrent latent dynamics models, which require step-by-step integration and accumulate error over long horizons, or (ii) neural operators, which enable direct prediction but are usually trained from initial conditions and do not explicitly enforce generalization from intermediate states. We introduce the Latent Evolution Operator (LEO), a parameterized map that takes a state at an arbitrary time, together with physical parameters and a forecast horizon, and predicts the future state in a single latent-space evaluation. Under standard manifold and regularity assumptions, finite-time evolution operators admit an encoder-propagator-decoder decomposition. We approximate this structure using neural networks trained on state pairs sampled across anchor times and horizons. We evaluate the method on the 1D Burgers' equation, a 2D advection-diffusion system, and the shallow-water equations. The model produces accurate predictions across parameters and time horizons, achieves significant speedups compared to Autoencoder-LSTM baselines, and maintains accuracy when initialized from intermediate states. These results indicate that learning finite-time evolution operators in latent space provides an effective alternative to recurrent latent dynamics models and operator learning methods trained only from initial conditions.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Rafiq, Wenjing Liao, Aditya G. Nair

item.title: Neural Operators Which Certifiably Simultaneously Solve Infinitely Many Convex Programs using Logarithmic Rank and Linear Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2508.14995v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural operators (NOs) are a class of deep learning models designed to simultaneously solve infinitely many related problems by casting them into an infinite-dimensional space, whereon these NOs operate. Such operator learning problems arise naturally in mathematical finance, for instance, when learning families of optimal portfolios or hedging strategies. Two significant gaps, however, remain between theory and practice: 1) most universal approximation guarantees do not describe practically implementable NOs or are pure existence statements; and 2) worst-case parameter bounds from universal approximation theorems suggest that constructed NOs may require an unrealistically large number of parameters to solve most operator learning problems, which stands in direct opposition to a slew of experimental evidence. This paper closes these gaps by exhibiting a short and simple training algorithm to construct a specific class of NOs, proximal equilibrium operators (PEOs), using (realistic) finite-dimensional deep equilibrium layers to solve families of convex optimization problems over a separable Hilbert space $X$. Here, the inputs are smooth, convex loss functions on $X$, and the outputs are the associated (approximate) solutions to the optimization problems defined by each input loss. Our main result is a certificate showing that, when the input losses lie in a suitable infinite-dimensional set, our PEOs trained with our algorithm do in fact uniformly approximate the corresponding solutions to arbitrary precision, with rank and width growing only logarithmically and the depth growing linearly in the reciprocal of the approximation error. We then validate both our theoretical results and the trainability of PEOs on three applications: non-linear PDEs, stochastic optimal control, and portfolio optimization and hedging problems in mathematical finance.
item.dc:creator: Anastasis Kratsios, Ariel Neufeld, Philipp Schmocker

item.title: Active-Set Identification in Noisy and Stochastic Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2509.00888v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Identifying active constraints from a point near a local minimizer is important both theoretically and practically in constrained continuous optimization as it can help identify optimal Lagrange multipliers and essentially reduce an inequality-constrained problem to an equality-constrained one. Traditional active-set identification guarantees have been proved under various types of constraint qualifications. Importantly, they also assume exact function and derivative values. This work extends such results to settings when both objective and constraint function and derivative values have deterministic or stochastic noise. Two strategies are analyzed. For each strategy, it is shown that, under constraint qualifications and other standard conditions, the active set of a local minimizer can be identified correctly when a point is close enough to the minimizer and the noise is sufficiently small. It is also shown that regularity of a minimizer is critical. Under strict complementarity, a fixed noise level suffices, whereas in the presence of a weakly active constraint the noise must vanish at least linearly in the distance to the minimizer in general, a rate that is also shown to be sufficient for correct identification. Guarantees are also stated for the use of active-set identification strategies within a stochastic algorithm, with explicit sample-size conditions. The theoretical findings are demonstrated with two simple illustrative examples and a more realistic constrained neural-network training task.
item.dc:creator: Frank E. Curtis, Daniel P. Robinson, Lara Zebiane

item.title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
item.description: arXiv:2609.39946v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $\Delta V(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{N\Delta V(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we check it against mean extinction times obtained without the action solver, i.e., from the backward equation of the jump process on a truncated lattice and from exact stochastic simulation. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $\Delta V(r)=\Delta V_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $\Delta V_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first, and at $r=1$ the barrier is 55% larger than $\Delta V_\infty$. A formal first-order expansion attributes this increase to the lag of the signal, of which the fluctuations of the signal remove a quarter. The saddle barrier $\Delta V(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, whereas the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply, by paths which keep the signal high and are usually followed by recovery. The mean extinction times of the backward equation, which include failed attempts, have a prefactor which tends to a constant, and they grow at a rate within $10^{-5}$ of $\Delta V(r)$ at every tested rate.
item.dc:creator: Mario Ayala, Johannes Zimmer
